rows.finding: Work-selection authority is contradictory and cannot represent the current global gate. The accepted adjudication assigns work selection to the state kernel, but the schema, generator, kernel, and tests require NOT_AUTHORITATIVE_DERIVED_VIEW; the generated restart block nevertheless calls the kernel the source of truth, while RUN_STATE later says the generated blocks are non-authoritative. The manually authoritative surfaces prohibit feature work until the comprehensive audit, yet the kernel has neither an audit task nor an active stop card and renders P2-004 as READY.

The ladder governs reports, slides, README/status prose, figure captions, and result tables, but reader_facing_surfaces scans only README.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md, top-level docs/contracts/*.md, and docs/run_reports/*.md. The new validator's own supported-row fixture satisfies every new required field yet lacks 19 fields that phase4 hard-requires; requesting all plus claim-index runs both validators.

rows.consequence: A valid L2 claim can be rejected or forced into less transparent wording even when its direction, boundary, repetitions, uncertainty, and floor clearance are supported.
rows.counterevidence: The conservative phrase rule prevents easy overclaiming, and the newer claim-index validator applies its directional-prose prohibition specifically to unresolved outcomes rather than every supported L2 row.
evidence_refs: behavior probe: PHASE4_FORBIDDEN.search('Condition A uses less energy than condition B.') => True
rows.finding: The legacy phase4 wording gate is stricter than the claims ladder because PHASE4_FORBIDDEN is level-insensitive. It rejects 'uses less energy' for every claim level, although L2 expressly permits a supported within-boundary directional difference after its evidence gates. The regression test mutates a legacy L1 row, so it does not test the valid L2 authority case.
